text: ...those looking for a classic adventure from the most famous agent will gag from this mishmash of explosions and speed, but those of us who want all this to serve to tell something more will be bitterly disappointed. [Full review in Spanish]
The most crucial and effective answer "Spectre" provides to combat the ominous expectations before it is talent.
Like Connery, it’s hard to say goodbye to such an iconic character.

The less said about Monica Bellucci’s part the better. Anyone from that quite large group of fans wishing for years for Bellucci to be in a Bond film will surely be furious at all she’s given to do here, and how little of it there is.
No longer tasked with putting the missing pieces of action, intrigue and effects together in our heads, the artifice of Bond is gone forever — and with it, any room for playful interpretation.
One of the best movies of the franchise is buried somewhere under the messy screenplay, but what can be found at the surface has much to appreciate.
I liked the movie, and I’m anxious to give it another look. But with this cast and this pedigree I can’t help but be disappointed with what we get.
Never mind the running time or overabundance of story; the film never bores, and the audience never loses interest. It simply isn't the wowing, visually illustrious film that its predecessor was.
Spectre is an immensely enjoyable Bond outing, that grows stronger with each passing viewing.
Daniel Craig's Bond story feels a little too sugary sweet for our beloved 007. Leave the happily ever afters for the fairytales, we came here for a movie about a spy.
Spectre never strays too far from the franchise formula but this action film is still a thrilling ride.
Spectre felt like loads of small ideas barely sewn together and a hasty attempt to make some sort of "ultimate villain" that doesn't work at all. Better than QoS at least...
An engaging two hours are then run into the ground for a wince-inducing final half-hour of unfortunate developments.

How much you enjoy this may depend on how you feel about Bond in general. If you miss the old days, with the world in elaborate peril and everything done with a big wink, this is a solid example of that.
Spectre, despite looking for all the world like a regressive throwback to Bond-eras passed, could end up pointing the way forward more acutely than we ever realised.

Daniel Craig has been a satisfying James Bond, but the films he's been put into have been, on average, far weaker than anything from the Connery, Moore, or Brosnan eras with this likely being the worst Craig film to date.
Great attention is given to making the CG disappear in favor of practical effects and authentic destruction, bringing back the amusement of older 007 adventures.
It's certainly not the worst Bond film in the world but it definitely misses the mark of being one of the best.

Like its predecessor, this is a densely-plotted thriller punctuated by exciting action sequences...The plot does get a little ahead of itself a few times, but it's pretty quick to recover and get things back on track.
Though it's a paint-by-numbers "James Bond movie," Spectre is still a James Bond movie, and as such, it's a pretty good time.
